purpose: LLM-facing extraction schema. One flat record per clause. The graph is built deterministically from these records afterwards — the LLM never emits nodes or edges.
unit_of_extraction: one Clause, passed to the LLM with its parent heading as context; the clause yields one record per distinct provision it contains

record.clause_id: string  // supplied by the parser, NOT by the LLM
record.provisions: array of Provision  // one per distinct duty, right, prohibition or statement in the clause; usually 1-3
record._note: v1.0 emitted a single flat record per clause. Measured against a page reading, that capped provision recall at 0.65: a clause imposing three duties became one node with one summary. The extraction unit is unchanged; what the clause yields is not.

provision_type.note: Pick exactly one — the dominant function of the clause.

actor.note: Who must act / who holds the right. null if none.

counterparty.note: Who benefits or is acted against.

Provision.summary: string  // one normalised sentence, max 25 words
Provision.trigger: string | null  // the condition or defined event that activates this, verbatim if capitalised
Provision.deadline: string | null  // verbatim, e.g. '30 days', '3 Working Days'
Provision.amount: string | null  // verbatim money or percentage, e.g. '£1,000,000', '1%'

refers_to.note: Other clauses/schedules named in the text. Leave empty — the parser fills this. Included only so the LLM does not smuggle references into summary.

Provision.uncapped: boolean | null  // true only where the clause expressly excludes a liability cap

llm_rules: Return exactly one JSON object per clause. No prose, no markdown fences.
Use null rather than guessing. A null field is correct; an invented one is not.
Never invent enum values outside the lists above.
Copy amounts, deadlines and defined terms verbatim from the clause. Do not normalise or convert.
summary must be a restatement, not a quotation of the whole clause.

deterministic_layer.note: Built by parser/regex before and after the LLM pass. No model involvement, no error rate.
steps: Split the PDF on schedule headings -> Document nodes.
Split on the numbering pattern (N.N.N, lettered limbs) -> Clause nodes with parent links and page numbers.
Gazetteer match every capitalised defined term in each clause -> USES_TERM edges.
Regex 'Clause N', 'Framework/Joint/Call-Off Schedule N', 'Paragraph N' -> CROSS_REFERENCES edges.

graph_materialisation.note: Mechanical transformation of records into the graph. Change this mapping, not the extraction schema, as the model evolves.
rules: each provision -> its own semantic node keyed `{clause_id}::{n}`; all of a clause's provisions point at the same (:Clause) via STATED_IN, so citations are unaffected
provision_type=liability -> (:Liability_Cap) with parsed cap_amount; uncapped=true -> EXCLUDED_FROM_CAP
amount/deadline normalisation (£1m -> 1000000 GBP, '30 days' -> P30D) happens HERE, not in the LLM

defer_until_v2: Lot scoping — add once you know whether queries actually cross Lots.
Service_Level / Service Credit modelling — only needed for Call-Off Schedule 14 questions.
ContractRole (Framework vs Call-Off role separation) — add when role ambiguity shows up in answers.
VARIES overrides (Scottish Law, MOD Terms, NI Law) — add when you start answering jurisdiction-specific questions.
Reified TRIGGERED_BY on edges — materialise Remedy instances per trigger instead.
